title: Cyber Capability Developer Technician
raw_text:
8-170D. Military Occupational Specialty 170D -- Cyber Capability Developer Technician
(Effective 202507)
a. Licensing/certification requirement. NA.
b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21.
c. MOS 170D. MOS 170D is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is any MOS.
Applicants from other military services (Air Force, Marine Corps, Navy, and Coast Guard) who
can substantiate their qualifications with performance evaluations, awards, and certificates are
encouraged to apply for MOS 170D. Non-military personnel (civilians), from all civilian sectors,
may apply for accession into the MOS, provided they too can substantiate their qualifications with
similar documentation. The proponent sets and maintains the technical qualifications for the
MOS. Please refer to https://recruiting.army.mil/170d/ for current selection criteria and Proponent
contact information. The Warrant Officer accessions process is available at
https://recruiting.army.mil/ISO/AWOR; please direct any accessions related questions to the
Warrant Officer Recruiting Branch at woteam@usarec.army.mil.
d. Associated SQI.
    (1) 0--No special qualifications.
    (2) 8--Instructor.
    (3) P--Parachutist.
    (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
    (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
Warrant Officer MOS)).
f. Qualifications.
    (1) All applicants must pass the MOS 170D Cyber Capability Developer Assessment (CCDA)
and must be nominated for MOS 170D by a current active-duty Cyber Capability Developer
Technician. The CCDA is offered once a year (August/September). The U.S. Army Cyber School
assumes responsibility for maintaining, administering, and scoring the assessment, as well as,
providing documented results to all applicants.
    (2) WO1/CW2 must--
         (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
         (b) Obtain a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET clearance with eligibility for access to
sensitive compartmented information (SCI), prior to Warrant Officer Candidate School
attendance.
         (c) Soldier must be capable of passing a counterintelligence scope polygraph (CSP) to
hold the MOS. Soldiers who refuse to take or fail a CSP will be reclassified.
         (d) Formal training (successful completion of 170D Cyber Capability Developer Technician
Warrant Officer Basic Course conducted under the auspices of the US Army Cyber School) is
mandatory. Waiver may be granted by Commandant, US Army Cyber School, Fort Gordon, GA
30905-5300.
         (e) Upon completion of 170D Cyber Capability Developer Technician Warrant Officer
Basic Course, WO1s incur a 6-year term of service obligation.
    (3) CW3 must—
          (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (2).
          (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Advance Course (WOAC) for CW2(P) and CW3.
    (4) CW4 must--
          (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (3).
          (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE) for CW3(P) and
CW4.
    (5) CW5 must—
          (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (4).
          (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
g. Duties.
    (1) WO1/CW2 must-
         (a) A Basic-level Cyber Capability Developer Technician is proficient in programming
languages at an intermediate level.
        (b) A Basic-level Cyber Capability Developer Technician has a basic-level understanding
of data structures, algorithms, object-oriented programming, secure design, operating systems,
x86 assembly, and SQL.
       (c) A Basic-level Cyber Capability Developer Technician is responsible for completing
assigned tasks and modules, as required and assigned to him/her by a Senior- or Master-level
Cyber Capability Developer Technician.
     (2) CW3 must--
       (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (1).

         (a) Manages, directs, and performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
         (b) Serve as a senior capability developer technical lead.
         (c) Executes capability development within a specialization area that aligns with their
certification (Unix, Windows, Radio Frequency, networks, embedded systems, data science, or
machine learning).
         (d) Identifies new and emerging technologies, capabilities, and threat capabilities that
affect cyber capability development efforts and focus.
         (e) Trains, coaches, and mentors basic-level cyber capability developers to increase
proficiency and prepare them for senior-level certification.
         (f) Identifies and recommends mitigation strategies for gaps in processes, skill sets,
access, capacity, and capability.
         (g) Develops and executes training for knowledge and skill gaps within the team.
         (h) Reviews and recommends adjustments to job qualification requirements and
certification to ensure relevance and currency.
         (i) Integrates cyber capability development into operational readiness assessments.
         (j) Directs team-level cyber capability development.
         (k) Manages team personnel.
         (l) Assigns tasking and coordinates development efforts across teams.
         (m) Interfaces with intelligence organizations and partners to synchronize cyber capability
development efforts.
     (3) CW4 must--
         (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (2).
         (b) A Master-level Cyber Capability Developer Technician has mastered their specialty
and is responsible for providing guidance and technical direction over multiple projects in this
specialty.
         (c) A Master-level Cyber Capability Developer Technician mentors Senior-level Cyber
Capability Developer Technicians as they progress to the Master level.
         (d) Master Cyber Capability Developer Technicians provide the highest level of technical
insight during the design of new software and hardware capabilities.
    (4) CW5 must--
         (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (3).
         (b) Directs capability development, integration, and management experience in support of
offensive and defensive Cyberspace operations and frameworks, at all levels.
         (dc) Ensure that doctrinal Cyberspace capability integration procedures and techniques
are taught at service schools and incorporated into Army, Joint and Coalition doctrine and training
literature.
         (d) Represent the Army and Cyberspace capability development activities at National and
International technology and leadership forums.
h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
    (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
    (2) Meet medical and physical standards per AR 40-501.
    (3) Table 8-170D-1. Physical requirements - A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump
(LJ) – 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and
Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles.
     (4) Authorized position titles are provided in appendixes B and C. The following grades are
used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals
 CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of
grade tables:
       (a) Table 8-170D-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE (Not Applicable)
       (b) Table 8-170D-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
